subject: Re: HealthScope model-fit & safety evals — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-28T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: HealthScope model-fit & safety evals — next steps

Hi Susan,

Thanks again for the time today — great to learn more about HealthScope's use cases and constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Recap:
- Primary workload: clinical triage & patient Q&A (high sensitivity to PHI; must refuse/route for PHI requests).
- Latency target: p95 < 250ms for short prompts (≤128 tokens) in the US region.
- Cost target: prioritize a model/config that balances throughput and operational cost (goal: ~50% lower per-token cost vs your current baseline).
- Evaluation needs: quality regressions on target prompts, refusal/safety rates for sensitive prompts, and model fit on HealthScope prompt sets.

Proposed next steps:
1) We'll run a two-week eval (suggested window: 2026-07-31 to 2026-08-14) using your representative prompt set and our safety/refusal harness.
2) We'll provide: recommended models & configs, bench reports (latency, token costs), and safety/refusal summary.
3) You confirm scope (which prompt buckets to include), whether evaluation data can be uploaded to the shared Drive link, and any procurement/contract requirements so we can provision Dedicated dev capacity if needed.

Initial model recommendations (based on what we discussed):
- redwood-neo-16b-quant (best balance: strong safety behavior, good long-context handling)
- redwood-7b-llama-quant (lower cost, faster throughput, acceptable quality on short prompts)
- open-7b-sft (for non-PHI low-cost paths; will require more guardrails)

I'll attach the prompt_set_v2 and a short model_eval_summary that includes our safety/refusal test buckets. Rafael/Vivek will follow up with technical details for canary deployment and quantization notes. 

Please confirm:
- Can your team share the prompt buckets by Friday 2026-07-30?
- Who on your side owns procurement/PO discussions (cc Mike if different)?

Thanks — looking forward to getting the eval started.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

--
Attachment stubs: prompt_set_v2.txt (text file of representative prompts), model_eval_summary.pdf (high-level report)

Subject: Re: HealthScope model-fit & safety evals — technical notes and guardrails

Hi Susan / Marissa,

Wanted to add the technical details you'll want for the evaluation and canary provisioning: 

Recommended configs for the eval (per workload):
- Clinical triage (short prompts, high safety sensitivity): redwood-neo-16b-quant, sequence length cap 512, kv cache enabled, int8 quantization. Expected p95 latency (us-east): ~180ms on a single A100-equivalent instance with batching disabled for low-latency tests.
- Patient Q&A (high throughput, fewer tokens): redwood-7b-llama-quant, batched 8x, int8; p95 ~120-160ms under moderate load.

Safety/refusal behavior and guardrail examples:
- Refusal template (explicit): "I can't help with requests that involve private patient information. Please reach out to your HealthScope clinical team or use the secure portal for PHI requests."
- Escalation hint (when classification uncertain): "This request may contain sensitive personal or clinical information. Would you like me to escalate to a human reviewer?"
- Input-sanitization stub: prefix-based stripping for any detected MRN/SSN patterns, and automatic redaction before logging.

Quality regression monitoring:
- We'll run prompt-level baselines and calculate a rolling MRR + refusal delta. If we see >5% drop in helpfulness for core prompts compared to baseline, we'll flag a regression.
- We will provide per-prompt diffs (CSV) and short sets of counterexample prompts for debugging.

Data & infra notes for the Private eval:
- We can support temporary VPC peering and a customer-controlled S3 for logs.
- Minimal control-plane access required by Redwood engineers for orchestration; we can sign an access-limited addendum if needed.

I'll include short example guardrail prompts in the shared Drive and attach the eval harness repo reference. 

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
